precepts.text: Be ye strong and let not your hands be weak, for your work shall be rewarded. When Asa heard the prophecy of Oded he took courage and put away the abominable idols out of all the land. That is what prophecy is for: courage to let go of idols and secret sins. As the war unfolds, more Israelites repent and wake up.
precepts.point: I will yet make doctrine to shine as the morning and pour out doctrine as prophecy, and leave it to all ages for ever. I have not laboured for myself only, but for all them that seek wisdom. We do not do this work for ourselves.

note.label: America At War With Iran: Preparation For Conflict

precepts.why:
When we teach the Bible and bring out the prophecy, in the street or in classes, what are these scriptures supposed to do for our people? The prophet told King Asa: “Be ye strong therefore, and let not your hands be weak: for your work shall be rewarded.” The days we are living in now are not the time for us to be weak.

“And when Asa heard these words, and the prophecy of Oded the prophet, he took courage, and put away the abominable idols out of all the land of Judah and Benjamin, and out of the cities which he had taken from mount Ephraim”. When Asa heard the words of the prophecy, he took courage.

That is what prophecy is supposed to do for us: give us the courage to let go of our idols and our secret sins. We are seeing prophecy unravel right before our eyes: Iran and Israel going to war, and now America getting involved. It was a rumor and talk for years, and now we see it unfold. That means more Israelites are repenting, and more of our brothers and our people are waking up. That is the doctrine poured out as prophecy, laboured for all them that seek wisdom.

precepts.point: That is why there should be no Christian church: Christ died only for Israel. Everything they quote about Gentiles and the world has already been shown to be Israel.

note.label: The Dividing Hatred: the Grafted in Strangers

precepts.why:
Paul writes to the saints at Ephesus, and the saints are the children of Israel. Yet he tells them, “Wherefore remember, that ye being in time past Gentiles in the flesh, who are called Uncircumcision by that which is called the Circumcision”. In time past the saints were called Gentiles. They were uncircumcised in the flesh because they had been walking “according to the course of this world”, raised in pagan customs, in idolatry. The Circumcision, cut in the flesh made by hands, is the southern kingdom.

“That at that time ye were without Christ, being aliens from the commonwealth of Israel, and strangers from the covenants of promise, having no hope, and without God in the world”. That sounds like Chronicles: “Now for a long season Israel hath been without the true God, and without a teaching priest, and without law.”

Who were they? “And he gathered all Judah and Benjamin, and the strangers with them out of Ephraim and Manasseh, and out of Simeon: for they fell to him out of Israel in abundance, when they saw that the Lord his God was with him.” The strangers are Ephraim, Manasseh and Simeon: the northern kingdom.

An alien is a stranger, a foreigner, the way they call migrants illegal aliens today. The ten tribes became aliens to the covenant, no longer part of the commonwealth of Israel, the nation, because they were cast off. The Lord told the northern kingdom, you are not my people, and I will not be your God: without God in the world. Those are the strangers Paul says are “no more strangers and foreigners, but fellowcitizens with the saints”. The northern kingdom got its citizenship back.

note.label: The Dividing Hatred: Cornelius the Centurion

precepts.why:
“Now for a long season Israel hath been without the true God, and without a teaching priest, and without law.” That is the northern kingdom: they stopped going to Jerusalem to worship, and Jeroboam set up idols for them. So when Asa gathered “all Judah and Benjamin, and the strangers with them out of Ephraim and Manasseh, and out of Simeon”, the northern tribes are called strangers. And “they fell to him out of Israel in abundance, when they saw that the Lord his God was with him.” Whenever Judah was on point, Ephraim would follow along.

The next king shows the same thing. Jehoshaphat, a good king of Judah, reigned from 870 to 848 BC. “And Jehoshaphat dwelt at Jerusalem: and he went out again through the people from Beer–sheba to mount Ephraim, and brought them back unto the Lord God of their fathers.” Who dwelt at Beersheba? Simeon: that was Simeon’s allotment of land. From Simeon’s land all the way to mount Ephraim, Jehoshaphat caused some of Ephraim to return back to the Lord.

“And he set judges in the land throughout all the fenced cities of Judah, city by city, And said to the judges, Take heed what ye do: for ye judge not for man, but for the Lord, who is with you in the judgment.” “Wherefore now let the fear of the Lord be upon you; take heed and do it: for there is no iniquity with the Lord our God, nor respect of persons, nor taking of gifts.” Jehoshaphat was a righteous king, and he set the law back in place.

So Israel was without God, without a teaching priest and without law, and the Lord would always use Judah to bring Ephraim back in, every single time. When Judah was on point, Ephraim followed along; when Judah went off, Ephraim went even worse off.

precepts.text: And he gathered all Judah and Benjamin, and the strangers with them out of Ephraim and Manasseh, and out of Simeon. The strangers out of Ephraim and Manasseh. Northern kingdom, they were called strangers.
precepts.point: Strangers. Strangers. Now, the literal definition of Gentiles is nation. How can you in time past be another nation? How can you in time past be another race? Go to sleep Japanese, wake up Arab. That does not make any sense. But when you are dealing with Christianity, it makes all the sense in the world.
precepts.why:
Paul says “at that time ye were without Christ, being aliens from the commonwealth of Israel, and strangers from the covenants of promise”. Who were the strangers? Chronicles shows it: Asa “gathered all Judah and Benjamin, and the strangers with them out of Ephraim and Manasseh, and out of Simeon: for they fell to him out of Israel in abundance, when they saw that the Lord his God was with him.”

The strangers out of Ephraim and Manasseh. That is the northern kingdom, and they were called strangers. Israelites, called strangers.

The literal definition of Gentiles is nation. How can you in time past be another nation? How can you in time past be another race? Go to sleep Japanese, wake up Arab? That does not make any sense. It only makes sense in Christianity. But when you read that Israelites of the northern kingdom were called strangers, Ephesians 2:12 makes sense: the strangers were Israel.

precepts.why:
“So then faith cometh by hearing, and hearing by the word of God.”

“when Asa heard these words, and the prophecy of Oded the prophet, he took courage”, put away the abominable idols out of Judah, Benjamin, and the cities he took from mount Ephraim, “and renewed the altar of the Lord.” Hearing the word gave him courage to act.

Hearing the word gives courage still, for we teach our people who they are, that the Israelites and the Christ are black. Faith comes by hearing.

precepts.text: If we seek the Most High He will be found, but if we forsake Him He will forsake us, the very charge Zechariah brought against Judah.
precepts.point: As Zechariah died he said, The Most High look upon it and require it. He prayed for vengeance on his murderer, and this is scripture; it is right to pray for the downfall of enemies who do much wickedness, even while we pray for the recovery and repentance of our own people.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 24: Joash Repairs the House and Then Falls

precepts.why:
The prophet went out to meet Asa and said, “The Lord is with you, while ye be with him; and if ye seek him, he will be found of you; but if ye forsake him, he will forsake you.” If we seek the Most High he will be found, but if we forsake him he will forsake us.

That is the very charge Zechariah brought against Judah: “because ye have forsaken the Lord, he hath also forsaken you.” They transgressed the commandments, so they could not prosper.

And as Zechariah died, he said, “The Lord look upon it, and require it.” He prayed for vengeance on his murderer, and this is scripture. It is right to pray for the downfall of enemies who do much wickedness, even while we pray for the recovery and repentance of our own people.
